newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet shares rise on mine study news.
newsitem.headline: Eramet shares rise on mine study news.

text.p: Shares in mining group Eramet rose strongly on Thursday as investors were relieved that chairman Yves Rambaud was kept in place while the government seemed conciliatory to the group.
Eramet was up 7.59 percent at 312 francs at 0908 GMT.
Eramet held a key board meeting on July 9 after months of difficult discussions with the previous government and its majority-owner, state holding Erap.
The previous government wanted to take away a mining licence on New Caledonia from Eramet to transfer it to a nickel smelter joint-venture of local Kanak interest and Canadian group Falconbridge.
The smelter project would give a boost to the New Caledonian economy and could soothe the Kanak independence movement ahead of a referendum on the island.

On Wednesday, the Eramet board issued a statement that it would propose a general meeting to name a new board -- including Rambaud as chairman -- which would also contain two personalities from New Caledonia.

The Prime Minister's office said that same evening it was ordering a study into the situation. It said it supported a project for a Kanak smelter but would also keep the interests of Eramet and its minority shareholders in mind.
"Rambaud is staying, that's good news, and the new government seems more conciliatory towards Eramet," a broker said.
